# Proverbs 26 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 26:1 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Like-snow in-summer and-like-rain in-harvest, so honor [is]-not fitting for-a-fool. |
| LOGOS | Like snow in summer or rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool. |
| PNEUMA | Honoring a fool is as out of place as snow in the summer or rain during harvest. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 26:2 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Like-a-sparrow for-wandering, like-a-swallow for-flying, so a-curse without-cause does-not-come. |
| LOGOS | Like a sparrow in its flitting, like a swallow in its flying, a curse that is causeless does not alight. |
| PNEUMA | An undeserved curse is like a fluttering sparrow or a darting swallow — it goes nowhere. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 26:4 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Do-not-answer a-fool according-to his-folly, lest you-be-equal — even you — to-him. |
| LOGOS | Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest you be like him yourself. |
| PNEUMA | Don't answer a fool on their terms, or you'll end up looking just as foolish. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 26:11 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Like-a-dog returning to-his-vomit — a-fool repeating his-folly. |
| LOGOS | Like a dog that returns to his vomit is a fool who repeats his folly. |
| PNEUMA | A fool who repeats their foolishness is like a dog going back to eat its own vomit. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

| LOGOS | As a door turns on its hinges, so does a sluggard on his bed. |
| PNEUMA | A door swings back and forth on its hinges, and a lazy person rolls back and forth on their bed. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

| Translator | Rendering |

| PNEUMA | A lazy person is more impressed with their own wisdom than seven people who give thoughtful answers. |
